title: Company handbook: Working at Redwood - roles, careers, benefits, onboarding, and tools
author: Ava Patel
content:
Overview

This document is the canonical Company Handbook reference for employees and new hires at Redwood Inference. It consolidates guidance on working culture, role definitions and career ladders, compensation/benefits highlights, the hiring and onboarding process, and a concise guide to the internal tools you will use every day.

Purpose
- Provide a single, up-to-date source of truth for people-ops, managers, and individual contributors.
- Standardize role expectations and career progression across engineering, product, and GTM teams.
- Reduce onboarding friction by centralizing steps, checkpoints, and access guides for internal systems.

Audience
- New hires (all levels)
- Hiring managers and interviewers
- People-ops partners and HRBP
- Engineering managers and team leads

1) Working at Redwood - culture and expectations

Intro
Redwood is a developer-first, production-focused company. We prioritize shipping reliable inference infrastructure and tooling with the same rigor we apply to productizing model capabilities. Our core cultural principles are: ship with empathy, measure impact, and operate with ownership.

Key expectations
- Results with craft: deliver high-quality work that balances speed and long-term maintainability.
- Customer-centricity: prioritize reliability, observability, and developer experience.
- Clear communication: asynchronous-first, document decisions, and use Confluence/Slack for coordination.
- Inclusive collaboration: create psychological safety, seek diverse perspectives, and mentor consistently.

Working model and time off
- Hybrid-first: flexible remote schedule with recommended in-office presence for onboarding and quarterly planning weeks.
- PTO: unlimited with recommended minimums and manager-aligned coverage plans. See the detailed PTO policy in HR portal for blackout dates and carry guidance.
- Parental leave: primary and secondary parental leave as described in the benefits summary below.

1.1 Code of conduct highlights
- Treat colleagues with respect; escalate concerns to your manager or people-ops.
- No retaliation for raising concerns.
- Security responsibilities: follow secure-SDLC guidance and immediately report suspected incidents to security@redwood.com.

2) Roles and career ladders

Overview
This section gives a concise mapping of role families, level expectations, and typical promotion criteria. Full competency matrices and interview rubrics live in People-ops shared drive and the manager toolkit.

Role families covered here
- Engineering (serving-runtime, infra, platform, dx)
- Product (PM, design, analytics)
- Applied ML and research
- SRE and reliability engineering
- Customer Success and Solutions
- GTM (sales, marketing)

Leveling summary (examples)
- IC-1 / Associate: learning role, contributes to tasks under mentorship.
- IC-2 / Engineer: owns implementation for features, reliable delivery.
- IC-3 / Senior: technical ownership of subsystems, mentors others, leads design.
- IC-4 / Staff: cross-team leadership, shapes product/architecture, drives alignment.
- IC-5+ / Principal/Engineering Manager / Director: strategic impact, large-scale ownership, organizational influence.

Promotion criteria (common signals)
1. Consistent delivery of impact aligned to role expectations.
2. Demonstrated growth in scope (technical complexity, cross-team influence).
3. Clear evidence of mentorship and knowledge transfer.
4. Manager and peer feedback, plus calibration in the leveling committee.

FAQs on leveling
- Q: How often can I be considered for promotion?
  A: Typical cadence is annual, with exceptions for rapid, demonstrable impact. Discuss readiness with your manager at least one quarter before desired review.
- Q: Who signs off promotions?
  A: Manager, peer reviewers, people-ops, and a cross-functional leveling committee.

3) Benefits and perks (summary)

Medical and financial
- Health: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans (US/EU region variants). Enrollment within first 30 days.
- Retirement: 401(k) with company match (US).
- Equity: Standard option grant at hire and periodic refreshes tied to role and performance.

Family and wellness
- Parental leave: 16 weeks paid for primary caregivers; 6 weeks for secondary caregivers (location-dependent).
- Mental health: EAP and mental health stipend for therapy sessions.
- Wellness: monthly stipend for home office or wellness-related expenses.

Work experience and learning
- Professional development stipend: annual allowance for conferences, courses, books.
- Internal learning: quarterly tech talks, onboarding bootcamps, and mentorship programs.

Perks and office benefits
- Commuter benefits where provided, free snacks in office hubs, remote equipment stipend, ergonomic assessments.
- Home office setup: one-time stipend and approved accessories ordering via Procurement.

How to access benefits
1. Login to the HR portal (hr.redwood.com) and complete new hire enrollment steps.
2. For region-specific questions, contact benefits@redwood.com.
3. For equity or payroll questions, contact finance-peopleops@redwood.com.

4) Hiring, interviews, and onboarding overview

Hiring principles
- Candidate experience and fairness: structured interviews, rubric-based evaluation, and clear communication of timeline.
- Speed with quality: minimize scheduling overhead while preserving rigorous technical assessment.
- Diversity and inclusion: use diverse interview panels and reduce bias with anonymized work samples where feasible.

Interview process (standard technical hire)
1. Recruiter screen: role fit and logistics.
2. Hiring manager screen: high-level scope and motivation.
3. Technical assessment: take-home or coding exercise depending on role.
4. On-site / virtual loop: 3-5 interviews covering system design, coding, product sense, and culture alignment.
5. Hiring committee review: calibration on role fit and compensation recommendation.
6. Offer and background checks.

Hiring matrix (time targets)
- Recruiter screen: 3 business days after application.
- Loop scheduling: within 10 business days of take-home completion.
- Offer: target within 5 business days of committee decision.

New hire onboarding checklist (first 90 days)
- Day 0-1: IT account provisioning, hardware delivery, HR paperwork, security training.
- Week 1: Team onboarding, ship first small task, buddy assigned.
- Week 2-4: Deep-dive onboarding meetings (runtime overview, infra walkthrough, product orientation).
- Month 1-3: 1:1 with manager weekly -> biweekly, set 90-day goals, first performance check-in at 90 days.

Manager responsibilities for onboarding
- Prepare clear 30/60/90 goals and success criteria.
- Ensure access to repositories, dashboards, Slack channels, and Confluence pages.
- Schedule recurring 1:1s and arrange early cross-team introductions.

5) Internal tools guide (quick reference)

Access and first steps
- SSO and identity: Okta is the single sign-on provider. New employees get an Okta activation email within 24 hours of hire.
- HR portal: hr.redwood.com for benefits, payroll, and time off.
- Engineering access: use the Onboard checklist to request repo access, Google Cloud projects, and Redwood Console demo access.

Common tools and purpose
- Confluence: canonical documentation and runbooks. Keep team docs updated and link decisions to ADRs.
- Jira: ticketing and sprint planning. Use Jira templates for incidents and RFCs.
- Slack: primary async comms. Use team channels and follow naming conventions (#team-*, #proj-*).
- GitHub: source of truth for code. Follow repo CONTRIBUTING.md and branch protection rules.
- Redwood Console (internal): feature flags, rollout control, per-route observability dashboards. Request demo account via eng-platform.
- Telemetry & logs: Datadog for dashboards and alerts; Loki for long-term logs.

Security and secrets
- Secrets manager: HashiCorp Vault for production secrets. Use approved SDKs for retrieval.
- MFA required for all access to prod systems. Do not share credentials or access keys via chat or email.

How to get help (tool-specific)
1. Check the team Wiki and Confluence first.
2. If you cannot find the answer, open a ticket in the respective team queue (eng-infra, eng-platform, security).
3. For urgent access needs, escalate to oncall-infra via PagerDuty and email infra-support@redwood.com.

6) Manager toolkit and recommended templates

Included templates (links to Confluence pages)
- 30-60-90 goal template
- Performance calibration rubric
- Interview evaluation rubric
- Offboarding checklist and knowledge transfer template

7) Policies and compliance highlights

Data handling
- Follow data-residency policies for customer data (see security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention).
- Do not upload customer data to public services without an approved DPA.

Privacy and confidentiality
- All employees sign NDA and data protection addendum. Treat internal documents as internal unless labeled otherwise.

8) Common questions and FAQs

Q: Who do I contact about payroll discrepancies?
A: payroll@redwood.com (cc: your manager and people-ops).

Q: How do I request additional equipment?
A: Submit an equipment request via Procurement portal; manager approval required for >$500 requests.

Q: Where do I find the tech on-call rota?
A: Confluence > eng-sre > runbooks > on-call schedule.

9) Ownership and maintenance

Document owner: People-ops (document custodian: Ava Patel)
Review cadence: annual review or triggered by major policy changes (e.g., benefits, local employment law updates).
Change process: Propose edits in Confluence, add reviewers, and publish after People-ops and Legal sign-off for substantive policy changes.
